en.html:
Case 1: The distant rumble

You'll make three calls in this case. Choose what you'd actually do on a real job, not what you think the course wants to hear. If a call goes badly, you'll see what happens and then get to make it again.

That's right. Out in the open, you can't make the crew safe, but you can make a strike less likely. Don't let anyone be the tallest thing around, keep everyone away from metal and water, use low ground or a dense stand of small trees, and get to real shelter as soon as you can. This is why the earlier calls matter: leave at the first sign of a storm so you never end up here.

The three right moves are to get away from metal, head for low ground (and watch for flooding), and get into a dense stand of smaller trees. Stay away from tall single trees, don't lie flat, and keep off equipment. Most of all, get the crew moving at the first sign of a storm so you never end up stuck in the open.
Not quite. Think about what lightning tends to hit (tall things) and what carries the current (metal and water). Try again.

en.html:
Three calls to remember

  1. If you hear thunder, stop work. Don't wait for rain.
  2. Shelter in a real building or a hard-topped vehicle, never a shed, a pavilion, or a tree.
  3. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back out.

en.html: Where is the nearest safe shelter? How long would it take your whole crew to reach it, and how will you warn them?

You make the call

As a crew lead, you're the one who decides when the crew stops work and when it goes back. With lightning, you often have seconds to make that call, and the rain usually hasn't started yet.

About 50 people are killed by lightning in the U.S. every year, and many more are left with permanent disabilities. Most work-related deaths are in farming and ranching, roofing, construction, and lawn care.

How this course works

  • Decide first. You'll face realistic storm situations before you're given any rules.
  • See what happens. Each choice plays out the way it could on a real site.
  • Plan for your crew. You'll finish by applying it to a site you run.

It takes about 8 minutes. You've probably watched a storm roll in on the job before, so bring that experience.

en.html:
1:40 p.m., commercial re-roof. Your crew of six is spread out across the roof and a metal scaffold. The sky overhead is still blue, but to the west the clouds are building and getting darker, and the wind has picked up. Then you hear a faint rumble of thunder. It hasn't rained at all, and the job is due to be finished by 4:00.

What do you do?

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: Ten minutes later, with still no rain, lightning hits the edge of the roof beside the scaffold. One roofer is thrown and badly burned, and the rest of the crew scrambles down in the open.

The lesson: if you can hear thunder, you're within striking distance. The first strike often comes before the rain does.

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: The storm moves in faster than anyone expected. Fifteen minutes later, your crew is still on the metal scaffold when strikes start landing nearby. In the rush to get down, one worker falls from the ladder.

The lesson: once there's thunder, don't start or finish any task the crew can't stop right away.

label.en: The pavilion, since it is closest
The client's warehouse
Under the oak, to stay out of the rain

en.html:
Good call. The crew is on their way down. Now you have to decide where to send them. Within reach, you have:

  • An open-sided equipment pavilion next to the lot, the closest option
  • The client's warehouse, a 3-minute walk away. It's fully enclosed, with wiring and plumbing.
  • A big oak tree at the edge of the lot

Where do you send the crew?

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: Lightning strikes close by and the current travels through the pavilion's metal posts. Two crew members leaning on the posts get a severe shock, and one ends up in the hospital.

The lesson: sheds, pavilions, tents, and covered porches don't protect you from lightning. Go to a fully enclosed building with wiring and plumbing. If there isn't one you can reach, use a hard-topped metal vehicle with the windows rolled up.

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: The oak is the tallest thing around, and lightning hits it. The current spreads to the crew sheltering underneath, and three of them are injured.

The lesson: lightning tends to hit the tallest objects. Stay away from isolated tall trees, poles, towers, cranes, and ladders.

label.en: "We're going back up now. The storm has clearly moved on."
"I'll send two people up to get started and keep the rest inside."
"We go back up 30 minutes after the last thunder. If we hear any more, the clock starts over."

en.html:
The crew is safe inside. The storm moves through. It's been 15 minutes since anyone last heard thunder, the rain has stopped, and the sun is out. The general contractor calls: "The sky's clear. Get your people back up there, we're behind."

What do you tell them?

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: Five minutes after the crew climbs back up, lightning from the tail end of the storm hits the building next door.

The lesson: going back outside too soon after a storm is one of the most common ways people get struck. Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.

label.en: Go back and make a different call

en.html:
What happened: Now two of your crew are on their own on a metal scaffold under the tail end of the storm. Sending fewer people up doesn't make it any less dangerous for the people you send.

The lesson: the 30-minute rule applies to everyone. Nobody goes back out early.

label.en: Finish the case

en.html:
Everyone goes home tonight. You stopped work at the first thunder, picked a real shelter, and waited the full 30 minutes. All three calls were right.

Next, you'll see why each of those calls matters and get answers for when your crew pushes back.

Case 2: No building in reach

The situation: Your landscaping crew is clearing brush on a large, open property, 15 minutes' walk from the trucks. The storm builds faster than the forecast said it would, and now the thunder is right overhead. Nobody can get to a building or vehicle in time.

Nowhere outside is safe in a thunderstorm. What you can still do is lower the risk.

Right. The forecast is your earliest warning. Move the high-exposure work to a different time, and make sure everyone knows where the shelter is and how long it takes to get there before the storm shows up.
Best plan: move the high-exposure work to the morning and brief the crew on where to shelter. Detectors can't catch the first strike, and you don't need to shut down the whole site.
Not the best plan. Think about what the forecast lets you do ahead of time. Try again.

en.html: Case 3, 6:30 a.m.: The NOAA forecast says thunderstorms are likely after 1 p.m. You have a crane lift and scaffold work planned for 2 p.m. What's the best plan?

Now plan for your own site

Your company's Emergency Action Plan should include a lightning protocol. On site, you're the one who makes it happen. Think of a site you're running now or will run soon.

1. Check before you start

Check the NOAA forecast (weather.gov) or NOAA Weather Radio before outdoor work starts. If storms are likely, think about moving the work to another time. Know which building is your shelter and how long it takes the whole crew to get there.

label.en: Check

en.html:
2. Watch the sky all shift

Darkening clouds and stronger wind mean a storm is building. Once you see those signs, don't let the crew start anything they can't stop right away.

label.en: Watch

en.html:
3. Thunder means stop

Any thunder means lightning is close enough to hit you, even if it's just a faint rumble. Stop work and move everyone to shelter immediately. Don't wait for rain or for a strike you can see.

label.en: Stop

en.html:
4. Use a real shelter

Best: a fully enclosed building with wiring and plumbing.
Next best: a hard-topped metal vehicle with the windows up.
Not a shelter: sheds, pavilions, tents, covered porches, or trees.

label.en: Shelter

en.html:
5. Wait 30 minutes

Stay in the shelter until 30 minutes after the last thunder. If you hear thunder again, start the 30 minutes over.

label.en: Wait

sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.fr: L'élément n'a pas été déplacé et reste en position {{position}}.
sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.it: L'elemento non è stato spostato e rimane in posizione {{position}}.
sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.nl: Het element is niet verplaatst en blijft in positie {{position}}.
sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.pl: Element nie został przesunięty i pozostaje w pozycji {{position}}.
sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.pt-PT: O item não foi movido e permanece na posição {{position}}.
sortingDragEndNotMovedAria.ru: Элемент не был перемещен и остается в позиции {{position}}.

sortingDragStartAria.de: Element aufgehoben. Es befindet sich derzeit in Position {{position}}. Verwenden Sie die Hoch- und Runter-Pfeiltasten, um es zu verschieben.
sortingDragStartAria.en: Item picked up. It is currently in position {{position}}. Use the up and down arrow keys to move it.
sortingDragStartAria.es: Elemento recogido. Está en la posición {{position}}. Usa las flechas arriba y abajo para moverlo.
sortingDragStartAria.fr: Élément pris. Il est actuellement en position {{position}}. Utilisez les flèches haut et bas pour le déplacer.
sortingDragStartAria.it: Elemento preso. È attualmente in posizione {{position}}. Usa le freccie su e giù per spostarlo.
sortingDragStartAria.nl: Element opgehaald. Het bevindt zich momenteel in positie {{position}}. Gebruik de pijltoetsen om het te verplaatsen.
sortingDragStartAria.pl: Element przyjęty. Jest obecnie w pozycji {{position}}. Użyj strzałek w górę i w dół, aby przesunąć go.
sortingDragStartAria.pt-PT: Item pego. Está atualmente na posição {{position}}. Use as teclas de seta para mover.
sortingDragStartAria.ru: Элемент взят. Он находится в позиции {{position}}. Используйте стрелки вверх и вниз, чтобы переместить его.
sortingDragStartAria.tr: Eleman alındı. Şu an {{position}} pozisyonundadır. Yukarı ve aşağı ok tuşlarını kullanarak taşıyın.

sortingDragUpdateAria.de: Verschieben des Elements von Position {{position}} zu Position {{newPosition}}. Drücken Sie die Leertaste, um zu bestätigen, oder die Escape-Taste, um abzubrechen.
sortingDragUpdateAria.en: Moving item from position {{position}} to position {{newPosition}}. press the space bar to confirm or press the escape key to cancel.
sortingDragUpdateAria.es: Moviendo el elemento de la posición {{position}} a la posición {{newPosition}}. Presiona el espacio para confirmar o presiona la tecla escape para cancelar.
sortingDragUpdateAria.fr: Déplacement de l'élément de la position {{position}} à la position {{newPosition}}. Appuyez sur la barre d'espace pour confirmer ou appuyez sur la touche escape pour annuler.
sortingDragUpdateAria.it: Spostamento dell'elemento dalla posizione {{position}} alla posizione {{newPosition}}. Premi spazio per confermare o premi escape per annullare.
sortingDragUpdateAria.nl: Element verplaatst van positie {{position}} naar positie {{newPosition}}. Druk op spatie om te bevestigen of op escape om te annuleren.
sortingDragUpdateAria.pl: Przesuwanie elementu z pozycji {{position}} do pozycji {{newPosition}}. Naciśnij spację, aby potwierdzić, lub escape, aby anulować.
sortingDragUpdateAria.pt-PT: Movendo item da posição {{position}} para a posição {{newPosition}}. pressione o espaço para confirmar ou pressione a tecla de escape para cancelar.
sortingDragUpdateAria.ru: Перемещение элемента из позиции {{position}} в позицию {{newPosition}}. Нажмите пробел, чтобы подтвердить, или Escape, чтобы отменить.
sortingDragUpdateAria.tr: Eleman {{position}} pozisyonundan {{newPosition}} pozisyonuna taşınıyor. Boşluk tuşuna basarak onaylayın veya Escape tuşuna basarak iptal edin.

sortingIncorrectPositionAria.en: This item should be in position {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.es: Este elemento debería estar en la posición {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.fr: Cet élément devrait être en position {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.it: Questo elemento dovrebbe essere in posizione {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.nl: Dit element zou in positie {{position}} moeten zijn
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.pl: Ten element powinien być w pozycji {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.pt-PT: Este item deve estar na posição {{position}}
sortingIncorrectPositionAria.ru: Этот элемент должен быть в позиции {{position}}

sortingInstructionAria.de: Drücken Sie die Leertaste, um dieses Element aufzunehmen und zu verschieben.
sortingInstructionAria.en: Press the space bar to pick this item up and move it.
sortingInstructionAria.es: Presiona el espacio para recoger este elemento y moverlo.
sortingInstructionAria.fr: Appuyez sur la barre d'espace pour prendre cet élément et le déplacer.
sortingInstructionAria.it: Premi spazio per prendere questo elemento e spostarlo.
sortingInstructionAria.nl: Druk op spatie om dit element op te halen en te verplaatsen.
sortingInstructionAria.pl: Naciśnij spację, aby przejąć ten element i przesunąć go.
sortingInstructionAria.pt-PT: Pressione o espaço para pegar este item e movê-lo.
sortingInstructionAria.ru: Нажмите пробел, чтобы взять этот элемент и переместить его.
sortingInstructionAria.tr: Boşluk tuşuna basarak bu elemanı alın ve taşıyın.
